entries.headline: ArgoCDTools README says the argocd-hook image's Terraform is unpinned; the Dockerfile pins 1.16.3
body: ArgoCDTools README.md:155 lists the image's Terraform as 'unpinned from the HashiCorp noble suite, as the iac image installs it'. argocd-hook/Dockerfile sets TERRAFORM_VERSION=1.16.3 and installs terraform=${TERRAFORM_VERSION}-1, and its comment says the version is pinned identically in three images and bumped together (AnsibleSpecs decisions.md, 'Terraform version'). The session's grounding G1 already flagged the line as stale. No phase of this slice edits it.
entries.consequence: A reader of the ArgoCDTools README is told that a rebuild of the hook image picks up whatever Terraform the suite serves, when it is pinned and must be bumped together with iac and kube-coder-iac-toolchain.
entries.proposal: fix now — one line in README.md:155, saying 'pinned (TERRAFORM_VERSION), bumped with the other two images'.
entries.author: plan-writer r1, planning, ArgoCDTools README.md:155 against argocd-hook/Dockerfile

entries.headline: Settle V10 after the operator's APPLY=true build of IaC/Destroy Stage against …
body: V10 — The operator's `APPLY=true` build against FieldnotesDeploy `dev` leaves the RBD image `fieldnotes-dev-data`, the PV `fieldnotes-dev-data-pv` and `argocd/FieldnotesDeploy/dev/` in TerraformState gone, and `config/dev/` deleted from FieldnotesDeploy (ANS-147's done-when).

`verification.json` marks V10 owed after: the operator's APPLY=true build of IaC/Destroy Stage against FieldnotesDeploy dev (Ruling D3). The run cannot take that action; settle the criterion once it has happened.
entries.consequence: V10 stays unproven until then; the test phase does not settle it.
entries.proposal: When that has happened, say so: the session settles V10 in verification.json.
entries.author: `verification.json`'s `owed_after`, seeded by the plan loop

entries.headline: JenkinsDeploy: the controller's jenkins-admin ClusterRole grants every verb on every core resource cluster-wide, Secrets included
body: Live on prd, ClusterRole `jenkins-admin` is `[{apiGroups: [""], resources: ["*"], verbs: ["*"]}]`, bound by ClusterRoleBinding `jenkins-admin` to `jenkins-prd/jenkins-admin`, the controller's ServiceAccount (JenkinsDeploy `chart/templates/jenkins-clusterrole.yaml`, `jenkins-deployment.yaml:28`). It reads every Secret in the cluster (`argocd-hook-credentials` in `argocd-hooks`, Argo's repo credential and OIDC client secret in `argocd-prd`) and creates pods in any namespace. argo-cd D1 says Jenkins holds no cluster credential, and D33/D41 bind the hook credentials to Argo's sync; Ruling Q1 overruled them narrowly for one dedicated identity, which reaches less than the controller already does. Seen while writing D66 in P1; the register says nothing about it. What the Kubernetes plugin actually needs (pods, pods/exec, pods/log in jenkins-prd, perhaps more) is not established.
entries.consequence: Code execution in the Jenkins controller (an admin's script console, a compromised plugin) reads every Secret in the cluster, the hook's credentials among them, while the argo-cd register states that Jenkins holds no cluster credential.
entries.proposal: card — scope the controller's role to what the Kubernetes plugin needs; a security change that needs its own proof across every pipeline, not this slice's.
entries.author: code-writer, P1, r1 — kubectl --context prd get clusterrole/clusterrolebinding jenkins-admin; JenkinsDeploy f3ee7df chart/templates/jenkins-clusterrole.yaml

entries.headline: Keep the Destroy Stage ServiceAccount's exclusivity a convention, or enforce it?
body: In effect, and recorded in D66 and D41 as amended (P1): only `Jenkinsfile.destroy-stage`'s pod spec names the dedicated ServiceAccount in `jenkins-prd` (Ruling D1), and nothing enforces that. prd has no ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and no webhook that checks `serviceAccountName` (only the cnpg, ESO and metallb webhooks), so any Jenkinsfile's pod spec can name it, and `jenkins-prd/default` can create Jobs in `jenkins-prd` (Role `jenkins-agent-jobs`) whose pods name it. Holding it means creating Jobs in `argocd-hooks` under `tf-presync` with `argocd-hook-credentials`.
- Keep the convention (in effect): costs nothing; whoever writes a Jenkinsfile in the estate can reach the hook's credentials.

- Enforce in the cluster: a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy in `jenkins-prd` that admits the ServiceAccount only on pods carrying something the pipeline alone sets. Nothing a Jenkinsfile cannot also set exists today, so this takes design, a JenkinsDeploy change and a test.
- Enforce in Jenkins: a Kubernetes cloud or pod-template restriction that only this job may use. Design in JenkinsDeploy's controller configuration.
entries.consequence: Write access to any Jenkinsfile in the estate reaches the hook's whole credential set through that ServiceAccount, which Ruling D1 meant to keep to one pipeline.
entries.proposal: keep — every Jenkinsfile that could name it lives in the operator's own repos, and the controller's jenkins-admin ClusterRole already reaches further; revisit with that defect's card.
entries.author: code-writer, P1, r1 — kubectl --context prd get validatingadmissionpolicies / validatingwebhookconfigurations; JenkinsDeploy chart/templates/jenkins-agent-jobs-role.yaml

entries.headline: Tell the operator, before a Destroy Stage build, that it deletes a repo's webhook which another deployed stage still relies on
body: Nothing is wrong today. Argo-cd D66 (decisions.md:464-465) and D39 as amended (:699-701) say that the webhook goes with the stage that manages it (manage_webhook). Neither says what happens to a stage of the same repo that stays deployed: it loses its push trigger. In KubeCoderDeploy the webhook belongs to dev (config/dev/terraform.tfvars manage_webhook = true; prd false, on both main and prd). A build against KubeCoderDeploy dev passes the guard, because the guard checks only REPO's STAGE. It deletes the repo's only hook, and prd's pushes then reach Argo only through D6's 30-minute refresh (ArgoCDDeploy config/prd/values.yaml:24). Nothing reports that the hook is gone. Two ways to cover it: a runbook note (P6 already covers the webhook bullet, and the plan now carries this fact for it), which tells the operator to move manage_webhook to the surviving stage and sync it before destroying the owner; or a guard or dry-run warning in Jenkinsfile.destroy-stage.
entries.consequence: Destroying KubeCoderDeploy dev while prd stays deployed deletes the repo's webhook without a word, and prd's deploys then start up to 30 minutes after a push instead of on the push.
entries.proposal: close — P6's runbook can say it, from the fact recorded in its plan section. A guard is worth it only if more repos put the webhook on a stage that is retired first.
entries.author: code-reviewer, P1, r1 — phases/P1/code_review_r1.md F1; KubeCoderDeploy origin/main 5b23a28 and origin/prd config/*/terraform.tfvars

entries.headline: The driver left a scratch clone at /work/scratch/JenkinsDeploy (`Target: github:pvginkel/JenkinsDeploy`)
body: The driver cloned (or adopted) `/work/scratch/JenkinsDeploy` for `Target: github:pvginkel/JenkinsDeploy`; the slice's phases for that repo are branched, merged and pushed there.

Deleting it is safe once the slice's commits are on origin — the push check before the doc phase confirms that. The close-out session removes it then and says so under this entry; nothing is asked of the operator. A clone left in place is synced by every later preflight in this environment and adopted by the next `github:` target naming that repo.
entries.consequence: none — the clone is where the run works; left behind, it takes disk space and a sync in every later preflight, until the close-out session removes it.
entries.author: the driver's target resolution

entries.headline: JenkinsDeploy: no gate pins that jenkins-prd/destroy-stage holds no grant in jenkins-prd
body: P2 adds chart/templates/destroy-stage-serviceaccount.yaml with no RoleBinding. JenkinsDeploy's test gate only renders the chart (helm template, tf-check, gen-architecture); it asserts nothing about RBAC, unlike ArgoCDDeploy's tests/render-chart.py, which P3 extends to pin the identity's two grants. If someone later binds destroy-stage in jenkins-prd, or adds it to the jenkins-agent-jobs RoleBinding beside default, the gate stays green.
entries.consequence: A later edit that widens the Destroy Stage identity inside jenkins-prd passes JenkinsDeploy's gate without a word; only review would catch it.
entries.author: code-writer, P2, r1, /work/scratch/JenkinsDeploy/.kubecoder/project.yaml

entries.headline: ArgoCDDeploy render gate: check_hook_namespace's docstring says argocd-hooks holds only the hook's credentials and identity
body: tests/render-chart.py:1527 reads "argocd-hooks holds a run's credentials and its identity, and nothing else (D33)". The assertion under it (1546-1557) now also requires Role/destroy-stage and RoleBinding/destroy-stage there (D66). The failure message was updated; the docstring was not.
entries.consequence: none — a reader of the gate is told the hook namespace holds less than the check enforces; nothing behaves differently.

entries.headline: Give KubeCoderDeploy's root variables defaults, so IaC/Destroy Stage can destroy its stages?
body: The destroy mode plans against the root's terraform, provider and variable blocks alone and exports TF_VAR_stage only: the stage's namespace went with its Application and is not an input of the run. KubeCoderDeploy declares `variable "namespace"` with no default (terraform/variables.tf), so a destroy of either of its stages fails at the plan with Terraform's "No value for required variable" and changes nothing. Once config/<stage>/ is gone, its zfs_dataset, zfs_quota, zfs_size and manage_webhook (no defaults either) fail the same way. FieldnotesDeploy's shared providers.tf (also KeycloakDeploy, StorageDeploy, JenkinsDeploy per grounding G4) defaults every variable. Options: defaults on KubeCoderDeploy's root variables, which nothing in the empty configuration reads; or the destroy run takes the stage's namespace as a fourth input.
entries.consequence: A Destroy Stage build against a KubeCoderDeploy stage fails at the plan and destroys nothing, until KubeCoderDeploy's declarations or the run change.
entries.proposal: card — take it when a KubeCoderDeploy stage is retired; defaults on its root variables are the smaller change and leave the run's contract alone.
entries.author: (KubeCoderDeploy origin/main terraform/variables.tf) and witnessed (its root reduced by presync.declarations passes terraform validate; a required variable with no value failing the destroy's plan is tests/test_destroy.py RealTerraformTests), code-writer, P4, r1, ArgoCDTools d7db58f

entries.headline: argocd-hook destroy: the kubernetes_manifest namespace read is pinned only against a hand-written state
body: presync/destroy.py _namespace reads a kubernetes_manifest's namespace at attributes.object.value.metadata.namespace, the {"value", "type"} wrapping a version-4 state gives a dynamic attribute (cty's JSON encoding, read in source, not run). tests/test_destroy.py feeds a hand-written instance in that shape; no test or run has read one Terraform wrote, because creating one needs a cluster at plan time. No deploy repo's Terraform declares a kubernetes_manifest today (they hold PVs, RBD images, ZFS datasets, CephFS subvolumes and webhooks).
entries.consequence: A destroy of a stage whose state holds a namespaced kubernetes_manifest, which no stage's does today, could try to delete it and fail with 403 instead of forgetting it, until the read is corrected.
entries.author: code-writer, P4, r1, ArgoCDTools d7db58f argocd-hook/presync/destroy.py
